xBRIEFInfo.description: Story xBRIEF for GitHub issue #2822 - one-time trusted-org install force-on for valueFeedback + productSignal enable.

plan.title: fix(value-feedback,product-signal): one-time org force-on at next install

narratives.Description: Trusted-org repos stay dark for local value-feedback and product-signal because typed `enabled: false` blocks org-auto (#2376) and productSignal has no org-auto layer (#2693). This story adds a once-per-checkout install/upgrade migration that force-enables local valueFeedback (enabled/emitEvents/sessionLine true; upstreamPrompt false) and productSignal.enabled for trusted-org consumers, with durable markers so later intentional opt-outs are not fought forever, without silently granting personal product-signal consent.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Add a once-per-checkout migration module under `packages/core/src/policy/` (value-feedback + product-signal force-on with durable markers under `.deft-cache/` or audited policy log) that forces local valueFeedback ON including subflags and sets productSignal.enabled=true for trusted-org origins, then wire it from the install/update refresh path in `packages/core/src/init-deposit/refresh.ts` (rebase onto #2818 if that PR still owns refresh). 2. Ensure post-force-enable missing/revoked product-signal consent triggers the D17 interactive consent ask on next interactive session/skill entry (headless fail-open); prefer `policy:clear-value-feedback` (or equivalent) so true opt-out/clear-key is distinct from baseline false. 3. Cover Part A/B ACs with focused tests in `value-feedback*.test.ts`, `product-signal` policy/consent suites, and CHANGELOG + docs for auditable source and post-migration opt-out.
narratives.UserStory: As a deftai org operator running directive update, I want trusted-org repos force-enabled once for value-feedback and product-signal, so that company dogfood collection and Insights eligibility start without hand-editing typed false baselines.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Part A: one-time valueFeedback force-on for trusted-org at install/upgrade (overrides typed enabled:false; forces subflags ON).
Part B: one-time productSignal.enabled force-on for trusted-org; consent still D17 interactive (not silent grant).

Refs #1709 #2376 #2693 #2603. Comment: enable-value-feedback must not leave emitEvents/sessionLine false.

items.title: Given a trusted-org repo with typed valueFeedback all-false, when update runs once, then local valueFeedback paths are forced ON with a durable marker.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a trusted-org consumer with a typed `plan.policy.valueFeedback` block of `enabled/emitEvents/sessionLine` false, when `directive update` (or install refresh) runs the once-per-checkout migration, then local valueFeedback is forced ON (`enabled`/`emitEvents`/`sessionLine` true, `upstreamPrompt` false), a durable marker is persisted so the force-on does not re-run forever, and `policy:show --field=valueFeedback` reports an auditable non-stuck-typed-false source.

items.title: Given the same trusted-org update pass, when migration runs, then productSignal.enabled is forced true without writing personal consent.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a trusted-org consumer with productSignal disabled or absent, when the same install/upgrade migration runs, then `plan.policy.productSignal.enabled` becomes true (default sink `deftai/product-signal` unless already overridden), the personal consent file is not auto-granted, and `product-signal:status` reports enabled=true while consent still reflects personal grant/revoke.

items.title: Given force-enable without consent, when the next interactive session or skill entry runs, then the D17 consent ask surfaces; headless stays fail-open.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a post-migration trusted-org repo with productSignal enabled and missing/revoked consent, when the next interactive session or product-signal skill entry runs, then the D17 first-time consent ask surfaces; when the same state is evaluated headless/CI, then no consent prompt blocks and fail-open behavior is preserved.

items.title: Given a later intentional opt-out after migration, when update runs again, then the marker does not re-force enable forever.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a repo that already consumed the one-time force-on marker and later intentionally disables valueFeedback or productSignal (or clears the typed key via a dedicated clear verb), when a subsequent update runs, then the migration does not re-enable against that intentional opt-out, and docs describe how clear-key vs explicit false vs disable verb differ.

items.title: Given a non-trusted-org repo, when update runs, then force-on does not enable either surface.

narrative.Acceptance: Given a consumer whose origin org is outside DEFAULT_AUTOENABLE_ORGS / DEFT_VALUE_AUTOENABLE_ORGS, when install/update refresh runs, then valueFeedback and productSignal remain OFF unless explicitly enabled, and no ambient product-signal consent nag is introduced.

expected_outputs: org force-on migration tests pass for valueFeedback and productSignal
durable marker prevents infinite re-force against later opt-out
